questions.question: If 45% of a number exceeds 20% of it by 48, then the number is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Percentage difference** between the two values = 45% − 20% = 25%

According to the question, this 25% corresponds to 48.

To find the **total number** (100%), we multiply by 4:

100% = 48 × 4 = 192

**∴ The correct answer is 192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**First percentage** of the number = 45%

**Second percentage** of the same number = 20%

**Numerical difference** between them = 48

**Formula Used:**

Number = (**Given Difference** ÷ **Percentage Difference**) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/38ec42abc5ad05cf944c13392dbc0b56f8fe035e686bfa2ebc2059f6e74b79b2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the required **number** be **x**.

⇒ 45% of **x** − 20% of **x** = 48

⇒ (45 − 20)% of **x** = 48

⇒ 25% of **x** = 48

⇒ (25 ÷ 100) × **x** = 48

⇒ **x** ÷ 4 = 48

⇒ **x** = 48 × 4

⇒ **x** = 192

**∴ The correct answer is 192.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Always remember common **fractional equivalents** for faster calculation: 20% = 1/5, 25% = 1/4, 40% = 2/5, 50% = 1/2, and 75% = 3/4.

Net Percentage Change

When a number is changed by two **successive percentages** a% and b%, the **net percentage change** is given by the formula: (a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100)%.

Base Value Concept

Percentage calculations are always relative to a **base value** (100%). If the base increases, the absolute value of the percentage also increases proportionally.

questions.question: An investment decreases by 30% in the first year, increases by 30% in the second year, and then increases by 20% in the third year. What is the overall percentage change from the initial value?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change for a decrease of **x%** followed by an increase of **x%** is always a decrease of (x²/100)%.

Step 1: Net change for −30% and +30% = −(30²/100) = −9%.

Step 2: Apply successive change formula for −9% and +20%: a + b + (ab/100).

⇒ −9 + 20 + (−9 × 20)/100 = 11 − 1.8 = 9.2%.

Since the result is positive, it is an **increase**.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.2% increase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First year decrease = 30%, Second year increase = 30%, Third year increase = 20%.

**Formula:** Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± r₁/100) × (1 ± r₂/100) × (1 ± r₃/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/869050b4513f71d0209ee999ff4d205c349c36062a6919d96dc62c06f26fb96e.png] 

⇒ Let the **initial value** of the investment be 100.

⇒ Value after the first year = 100 − 30% of 100 = 70.

⇒ Value after the second year = 70 + 30% of 70 = 70 + 21 = 91.

⇒ Value after the third year = 91 + 20% of 91 = 91 + 18.2 = 109.2.

⇒ **Overall percentage change** = (Final Value − Initial Value) ÷ Initial Value × 100

⇒ Net change = (109.2 − 100) ÷ 100 × 100 = 9.2%.

**∴ The correct answer is 9.2% increase.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Formula

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective net change is given by (a + b + ab/100)%.

Fraction Method for Multi-Step Changes

Convert percentages to fractions (e.g., 20% = 1/5). For an increase, multiply by (1 + 1/5) = 6/5; for a decrease, multiply by (1 − 1/5) = 4/5.

Inverse Percentage Change

If a value increases by r%, it must decrease by [r/(100 + r)] × 100% to return to the original value.

questions.question: There are 400 multiple choice questions in a test. 4 marks are allotted for a correct answer and 1 mark is deducted for a wrong answer or unattempted question from total score of correct answers. If a candidate has scored 1280 marks in the test, how many questions did the candidate answer correctly?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume all **400 questions** are correct: 400 × 4 = **1600 marks**.

Actual score = **1280 marks**; Difference = 1600 − 1280 = **320 marks**.

Loss per wrong/unattempted question = 4 (marks not gained) + 1 (penalty) = **5 marks**.

Number of wrong/unattempted questions = 320 ÷ 5 = **64**.

Number of **correct questions** = 400 − 64 = **336**.

**∴ The correct answer is 336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total questions = **400**

Marks for **correct answer** = **+4**

Marks for **wrong/unattempted** = **−1**

Total score obtained = **1280**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b8c0713be3362a89e533a99aa2aeb165d73db1e3af9e9f3608eb24bf274011ff.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Score = (Number of Correct Answers × Marks per Correct) − (Number of Incorrect Answers × Negative Marks)

**Calculations:**

Let the number of **correctly answered** questions be **C**.

Let the number of **wrong or unattempted** questions be **W**.

⇒ C + W = 400 --- (i)

⇒ 4C − 1W = 1280 --- (ii)

Adding equations (i) and (ii):

⇒ (C + W) + (4C − W) = 400 + 1280

⇒ 5C = 1680

⇒ C = 1680 ÷ 5

⇒ C = 336

**∴ The correct answer is 336.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Negative Marking Effect

For every wrong answer, the net loss is the sum of the positive marks and the penalty (e.g., 4 + 1 = 5). This is used in the "Assumption Method" to find the total incorrect count.

Accuracy Calculation

Accuracy % = (Number of Correct Answers ÷ Total Questions Attempted) × 100. In this case, since unattempted also carry a penalty, the base is the total 400 questions.

Alligation Method

This can be solved by comparing the average marks per question (1280 ÷ 400 = 3.2) against the individual marks (+4 and −1) to find the ratio of correct to wrong questions.

questions.question: If the amount payable after 2 years is 1.1025 times of the sum invested, at compound interest (compounded annually), what is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for **2 years** = Amount ÷ Principal = 1.1025

Multiplying factor for **1 year** = √1.1025 = 1.05

**Rate of interest** = (1.05 − 1) × 100 = 0.05 × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time (n) = **2 years**

Amount (A) = 1.1025 × **Principal (P)**

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/14a94cdab7b02007497d5f2639c7d407f64797185745ecaf8c8540e31d0f2d42.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1.1025 × P = P(1 + r/100)²

⇒ 1.1025 = (1 + r/100)²

⇒ √1.1025 = 1 + r/100

⇒ 1.05 = 1 + r/100

⇒ r/100 = 1.05 − 1

⇒ r/100 = 0.05

⇒ r = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Rule

For two years, if the annual rate is r%, the **effective rate** is given by r + r + (r × r)/100.

Amount for n years

When interest is **compounded annually**, the total amount after n years is A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ.

Multiplying Factor

If a sum grows by r% every year, it is multiplied by (1 + r/100) each year. For 2 years, the factor is (1 + r/100)².

questions.question: In an apartment complex, the monthly electricity consumption (in units) for five flats is 320, 400, 360, 340, and 380. If the residents want to know the average monthly consumption (in units) per flat by using the direct method, what value will they obtain?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **Assumed Mean** of 360.

Calculate deviations: (320−360), (400−360), (360−360), (340−360), (380−360)

Net Deviation = (−40) + (+40) + (0) + (−20) + (+20) = 0

**Average** = Assumed Mean + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Flats) = 360 + (0 ÷ 5) = 360

**∴ The correct answer is 360 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Monthly consumption of **five flats** are 320, 400, 360, 340, and 380 units.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ecd488a0fcb8bd9966dea3497081d86557feeee8cd396f43251a0a88a70bb7b4.png] 

⇒ **Total Consumption** = 320 + 400 + 360 + 340 + 380

⇒ Total Consumption = 1800 units

⇒ **Number of Flats** = 5

⇒ **Average** = 1800 ÷ 5

⇒ Average = 360 units

**∴ The correct answer is 360 units.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean

It is the most common measure of central tendency, calculated as Σx ÷ n, where Σx is the sum of values and n is the count.

Properties of Mean

The sum of **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero.

Combined Average

If two groups have sizes n₁, n₂ and averages a₁, a₂, then the **combined average** is (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

questions.question: A trader initially marks all his goods 60% above the cost price. He sells half of the goods at a discount of 25% on the marked price. For the remaining half, he revises the marked price to 80% above the cost price and then offers a discount of 30%. Find the overall profit percentage earned by the trader.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net profit % on 1st half = 60 − 25 − (60 × 25) ÷ 100 = 20%

Net profit % on 2ⁿd half = 80 − 30 − (80 × 30) ÷ 100 = 26%

Since both halves are equal in quantity, average profit is calculated.

Overall Profit % = (20% + 26%) ÷ 2 = 23%

**∴ The correct answer is 23%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **markup percentage** = 60%

Revised **markup percentage** for second half = 80%

**Discount** on first half = 25% | **Discount** on second half = 30%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 + Markup %)/100 × (100 − Discount %)/100

Overall Profit % = [(Total SP − Total CP) ÷ Total CP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/471b55152a982446d5a25fe4a149e0c18831d252f9a58a9183c5f39955ddcd7e.png] 

Let the total quantity be 2 units and **cost price** of each unit be 100.

⇒ Total **Cost Price** = 2 × 100 = 200

⇒ **Selling Price** of 1st unit = 100 × (160/100) × (75/100) = 120

⇒ **Selling Price** of 2ⁿd unit = 100 × (180/100) × (70/100) = 126

⇒ Total **Selling Price** = 120 + 126 = 246

⇒ Total **Profit** = 246 − 200 = 46

⇒ **Overall Profit Percentage** = (46 ÷ 200) × 100 = 23%

**∴ The correct answer is 23%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Net Percentage Change

When a value changes by x% and then by y%, the net percentage change is given by the formula x + y + (xy ÷ 100). In profit-loss, markup is positive and discount is negative.

CP, MP, and Profit Relationship

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly calculated as MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit %) ÷ (100 − Discount %).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂ ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: An article is sold at a loss of 12% on its cost price. If the same article were sold for ₹84 more than its original selling price, the seller would make a profit of 8% on the same cost price. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The difference between a 12% **Loss** and an 8% **Profit** is 12% + 8% = 20%.

Given that this 20% difference is equal to ₹84.

20% of **Cost Price (CP)** = ₹84.

100% (Total CP) = 84 × 5 = ₹420.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Loss** = 12%

New **Profit** = 8%

Increase in **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹84

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss)%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/854f4f3b021a322d828e8c9d77f8c3cb5c337d5ef7e8a5c7daf3018cfb2a23d5.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = 100 − 12 = 88 units.

⇒ New Selling Price (SP₂) = 100 + 8 = 108 units.

⇒ Difference in **Selling Price** = 108 − 88 = 20 units.

⇒ 20 units = ₹84.

⇒ 1 unit = 84 ÷ 20 = ₹4.2.

⇒ 100 units (CP) = 4.2 × 100 = ₹420.

⇒ Therefore, the **Cost Price** of the article is ₹420, which corresponds to **Option 2**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Cost Price

Unless stated otherwise, profit or loss percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. Formula: Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Relation between CP and SP

If there is a profit of P%, then SP = CP × (100 + P)/100. If there is a loss of L%, then SP = CP × (100 − L)/100.

Marked Price and Discount

**Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount. MP = CP + Markup.

questions.question: A rectangular garden has a length of 16 meters and a width of x meters. If the width is the mean proportional between 4 meters and 64 meters, what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **mean proportional** of two numbers a and b is calculated as √(a × b).

Here, a = 4 and b = 64.

Value of x = √(4 × 64) = √256 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the **rectangular garden** = 16 m

Width of the **rectangular garden** = x m

Numbers for **mean proportional** = 4 m and 64 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ea1a840eeb901cb68b99871d539e745852f25ad2c4491ce0e4b733e927a8ca92.png] 

**Formula Used:**

If x is the **mean proportional** between a and b, then a : x :: x : b

⇒ a/x = x/b

⇒ x² = a × b

**Calculations:**

⇒ x² = 4 × 64

⇒ x² = 256

⇒ x = √256

⇒ x = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is the square root of their product: x = √(a × b).

Third Proportional

If a, b, and c are in continued proportion (a : b :: b : c), then c is the third proportional: c = b² ÷ a.

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then d is the fourth proportional: d = (b × c) ÷ a.

questions.question: Four prime numbers are listed in order. If the product of the first three is 105 and the product of the last three is 385, what is the largest prime number?

Ratio of products = (p₁ × p₂ × p₃) ÷ (p₂ × p₃ × p₄) = 105 ÷ 385.

Common factors p₂ and p₃ cancel out, leaving p₁ ÷ p₄ = 105 ÷ 385.

Simplifying the fraction: 105 ÷ 385 = 21 ÷ 77 = 3 ÷ 11.

Since the numbers are **prime numbers** listed in order, we have p₁ = 3 and p₄ = 11.

questions.question: Seven years ago Ramu was five times as old as his son. The present age difference between Ramu and his son is 28 years. Find the sum of their present ages.

questions.question: If the consecutive angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio 2:3, what is the measure of the smaller angle?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The sum of the **ratio parts** is 2 + 3 = 5.

Since **consecutive angles** of a **parallelogram** are **supplementary**, their sum is 180°.

⇒ 5 units = 180°

⇒ 1 unit = 36°

⇒ Smaller angle = 2 units = 2 × 36° = 72°.

**∴ The correct answer is 72°.**

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2x + 3x = 180°

⇒ 5x = 180°

⇒ Smaller angle = 2x = 2 × 36°

⇒ Smaller angle = 72°

⇒ Larger angle = 3x = 3 × 36° = 108°

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Distance** = L₁ + L₂ = 250 + 300 = 550 m

⇒ Relative Speed = 10 × 5 = 50 m/s

⇒ **Time to cross** = 550 ÷ 50

⇒ Time = 11 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 11 sec.**

• **1 Watt-second** is exactly equal to **1 Joule**; thus, **1 kWh** is also **3.6 × 10⁶ Joules** or **3.6 Megajoules (MJ)**.
 
 
 
• **Electric Power:**
 
 
• Defined as the rate at which **electrical work** is done or the rate at which **electrical energy** is transferred by an electric circuit.
 
• Commonly calculated using the product of **Voltage (V)** and **Current (I)**, represented as **P = V × I**.

• **Liberalisation** in the context of the **1991 Economic Reforms** refers to the relaxation of government restrictions on economic activities to provide more freedom to **private enterprises**.

• The reforms aimed to integrate the Indian economy with the global market by reducing **import duties**, removing **quantitative restrictions** (quotas) on trade, and simplifying **foreign exchange** regulations.
 
• By removing these barriers, the government sought to encourage **competition**, improve **industrial efficiency**, and attract **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** to modernize the domestic production base.
 
• The policy shift was triggered by a severe **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis in **1991**, necessitating a move away from the inward-looking, protectionist policies of the previous decades.

• **Globalisation:** Focused on increasing the **international reach** of the economy, which included encouraging rather than banning **foreign companies**.
 
• **Deregulation:** The **MRTP Act** (Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act) was amended to remove the requirement for large companies to seek prior government approval for expansion, thereby decreasing **government control**.

questions.question: Which factors are responsible for the increase in metallic character down a group in the periodic table?

options.text: Increasing atomic size and constant ionization energy
Decreasing ionization energy and increasing atomic size
Increasing ionization energy and decreasing atomic size
Constant ionization energy and decreasing atomic size

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decreasing ionization energy and increasing atomic size**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Metallic character** represents the level of reactivity of a metal and its ability to lose **valence electrons** to form **positive ions** (cations).
 
• As we move down a **group** in the **modern periodic table**, the number of **energy shells** increases progressively with each period.
 
• This addition of shells leads to a significant increase in **atomic size** (atomic radius), which places the outermost electrons further away from the positively charged **nucleus**.
 
• The **shielding effect** of inner-shell electrons also increases down the group, further reducing the **effective nuclear charge** exerted on the valence electrons.
 
• Due to the increased distance and reduced attraction, the **ionization energy**—the energy required to remove the most loosely bound electron—decreases down the group.
 
• Since electrons are lost more easily when ionization energy is low, the tendency to exhibit **electropositive** behavior grows, resulting in an increase in **metallic character**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trends across a Period:**

 
 
• Across a period from left to right, the **metallic character** decreases because the atomic size decreases and the **nuclear charge** increases, making it harder to lose electrons.
 
• Elements on the extreme left of the periodic table (**Alkali Metals**) possess the highest metallic character in their respective periods.
 
 
 
• **Electronegativity:**
 
 
• Metals generally have **low electronegativity** and **low electron affinity** compared to non-metals.
 
• The increase in metallic character is accompanied by a decrease in **non-metallic character** and oxidizing power.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactivity:**
 
 
• For metals, **chemical reactivity** increases down a group as it becomes easier to form ions, whereas for non-metals, reactivity typically decreases down a group.

questions.question:
Which statement about Application Software is True or False?

(i) Application Software depends on System Software like the OS to be loaded and access hardware.

(ii) The failure of one application always causes the OS to crash.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i) True, (ii) False**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Statement (i) explains the structural dependency of software. **Application Software** is designed to perform specific tasks for the user but lacks the low-level instructions to manage hardware components directly. It relies on **System Software**, specifically the **Operating System (OS)**, to act as an intermediary for resource allocation, memory management, and hardware communication. ***Hence, statement (i) is correct.***
 
• Statement (ii) discusses the robustness of modern computing environments. Modern **Operating Systems** implement **Process Isolation** and **Protected Memory** architectures. Each application runs in a separate memory space, which prevents the failure or crash of a single application from affecting the **OS Kernel** or other active processes. Users can typically close the failed application without rebooting the entire system. ***Hence, statement (ii) is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Application Software**

 
 
• Function: Performs specific end-user tasks such as document creation, data analysis, or entertainment.
 
• Types: Includes **General Purpose** (Word Processors), **Specialized** (Accounting Software), and **Custom-built** solutions.
 
• Examples: **Microsoft Office**, **Adobe Photoshop**, and **Web Browsers** like Chrome or Firefox.
 
 
 
• **System Software**
 
 
• Function: Coordinates hardware operations and provides a platform for application execution.
 
• Components: Includes the **Operating System**, **BIOS/UEFI**, **Device Drivers**, and **Utility Programs**.
 
• Key Roles: Responsible for **Process Management**, **File System** control, and ensuring **System Security**.

questions.question: What is the term of an elected MLA in Indian State Legislatures, unless dissolved prematurely?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• As per **Article 172** of the **Constitution of India**, the normal tenure of the **Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha) of every state is **5 years**.
 
• The duration of this **five-year term** is calculated from the date appointed for the **first meeting** of the assembly after the general elections are concluded.
 
• An **MLA (Member of the Legislative Assembly)** is a representative directly elected by the adult voters of a specific **electoral constituency** to represent them in the state legislature.
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** stands automatically dissolved at the end of the five-year period; however, the **Governor** of the state has the executive power to dissolve the assembly prematurely under specific constitutional circumstances, such as a **No-Confidence Motion** or a breakdown of constitutional machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Constitutional Amendments**:

questions.question: Which law governs the relationship between the pressure and volume of a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Boyle's Law**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boyle's Law**, named after the physicist **Robert Boyle** who published it in **1662**, describes the **isothermal** relationship in gases.
 
• It states that the **absolute pressure** exerted by a given mass of an **ideal gas** is **inversely proportional** to the **volume** it occupies, provided the **temperature** and **amount of gas** remain **constant** within a closed system.
 
• Mathematically, the law is expressed as **P ∝ 1/V**, which means the product of pressure (P) and volume (V) is a constant (k): **PV = k**.
 
• When comparing a gas under two different sets of conditions at the same temperature, the formula **P₁V₁ = P₂V₂** is utilized to calculate unknown variables.
 
• According to the **kinetic molecular theory**, as volume decreases, the **gas molecules** are crowded into a smaller space, increasing the frequency of collisions with the container walls, which results in higher **pressure**.
 
• A graphical representation of this law on a pressure-volume graph produces a curve known as an **isotherm**, which is a rectangular hyperbola.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charles's Law**:

 
 
• Formulated by **Jacques Charles**, it states that the **volume** of a fixed mass of gas is **directly proportional** to its **absolute temperature** (in Kelvin) when the **pressure** is kept constant.
 
• The mathematical relation is **V/T = k** or **V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂**.
 
 
 
• **Gay-Lussac's Law**:
 
 
• Developed by **Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac**, it establishes that the **pressure** of a gas is **directly proportional** to its **absolute temperature** when the **volume** remains constant.
 
• The formula is **P/T = k** or **P₁/T₁ = P₂/T₂**.
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Law**:
 
 
• Proposed by **Amedeo Avogadro**, it states that **equal volumes** of all gases, at the same **temperature and pressure**, contain the same **number of molecules** (or moles).
 
• This indicates that the **volume** is directly proportional to the **number of moles** (n), expressed as **V/n = k**.

questions.question: What was the Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955, renamed as in 1976?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

• The **Untouchability (Offences) Act, 1955** was enacted by the **Parliament of India** to prescribe punishments for the practice of untouchability, fulfilling the mandate of **Article 17** of the **Constitution**.
 
• In **1976**, based on the recommendations of the **Elayaperumal Committee** (1965), the act was comprehensively amended to make its provisions more stringent and effective.
 
• The amendment officially changed the title of the legislation to the **Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955**, shifting the focus from merely penalizing offences to actively protecting the **civil rights** of marginalized communities.

• The act is applicable to the whole of **India** and covers discriminatory practices in public places such as **temples**, **hotels**, **hospitals**, and **educational institutions**.

• **Article 35**:

questions.question: Which of the following architectural techniques was introduced to India during the Sultanate period?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arch and dome construction technique**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The arrival of the **Delhi Sultanate** in the **13th century** introduced the **Arcuate style** of architecture, which prominently featured the **Arch and dome construction technique**.
 
• Prior to this period, Indian architecture primarily followed the **Trabeate style**, which relied on horizontal beams supported by vertical columns (slab-and-beam).
 
• The **true arch** was a major structural innovation that utilized a central **keystone** to distribute the weight of the roof outwards and downwards to the pillars, rather than relying on the strength of a single horizontal stone.
 
• The **Dome** allowed for the creation of massive, column-free internal spaces, which were aesthetically grand and functional for **congregational prayers** in **mosques**.
 
• These large-scale constructions were supported by the introduction of **high-quality lime mortar** as a binding agent, which offered superior strength and durability compared to the **mud or dry masonry** used in earlier periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slab-and-beam roofing:**

 
 
• This is also known as the **Trabeate style** and was the traditional method for constructing **Hindu**, **Buddhist**, and **Jain** temples.
 
• It was limited by the tensile strength of the materials, meaning large rooms required many supporting pillars.
 
 
 
• **Key Architectural Examples:**
 
 
• The **Alai Darwaza**, built by **Alauddin Khilji** in **1311 AD**, is the first building in India to employ the **true arch** and scientific dome principles perfectly.
 
• The **Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque** and the **Qutub Minar** complex showcase the transition from **corbelled arches** (made by local craftsmen using older techniques) to the fully developed **Arcuate** forms.
 
• Other features introduced during this period include the use of **minarets**, **calligraphy** for decoration, and **arabesque** patterns.

questions.question: What change occurs in the amount of heat produced when the electric current in a conductor is doubled?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four times**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between the heat generated in a conductor and the electric current flowing through it is defined by **Joule's Law of Heating**.
 
• According to this physical law, the **heat produced (H)** in a resistor is **directly proportional** to the **square of the electric current (I)** passing through it, provided the **resistance (R)** and **time (t)** remain constant.
 
• The fundamental formula for calculating the thermal energy is **H = I²Rt**.
 
• When the electric current is **doubled**, the new current (I') becomes **2I**.
 
• Substituting the value of the new current into the formula gives the new heat output (H') as: **H' = (2I)² × R × t**.
 
• Simplifying the expression results in **H' = 4 × I²Rt**, which indicates that the heat produced is exactly **four times** the initial amount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Factors of Joule Heating**:

 
 
• **Resistance (R)**: Measured in **Ohms**, it represents the opposition to electron flow. Increasing resistance while keeping current constant results in a linear increase in heat.
 
• **Current (I)**: Measured in **Amperes**, it has the most significant impact on heat because of the squared relationship in the formula.
 
• **Time (t)**: Measured in **seconds**, the total thermal energy is directly proportional to the duration of the current flow.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Domestic Applications**:
 
 
• **Heating Elements**: Devices like **electric heaters** and **geysers** use high-resistance alloys like **Nichrome** to maximize heat production.
 
• **Safety Mechanisms**: An **electric fuse** is designed to melt and break the circuit if the current becomes dangerously high, preventing fires caused by excessive heating.
 
• **Incandescent Bulbs**: The **Tungsten filament** is heated to a very high temperature to emit light, demonstrating the practical conversion of electrical energy into thermal and radiant energy.

questions.question: Which latitude experiences the longest daylight during the June solstice?

__
 
• The **June solstice**, also known as the **Summer Solstice** in the Northern Hemisphere, occurs around **June 21** each year when the Earth's **North Pole** is tilted at its maximum angle of approximately **23.5 degrees** toward the Sun.
 
• During this event, the Sun's rays are perpendicular to the **Tropic of Cancer** (23½degree N), resulting in the longest day of the year for the **Northern Hemisphere**.
 
• The duration of daylight increases as one moves further **north** from the Equator during the June solstice; while the Equator receives about 12 hours of light, latitudes further north experience significantly longer periods.
 
• At the **Arctic Circle**, located at **66½degree N**, the Sun does not set at all for a full **24-hour period**, a phenomenon famously known as the **Midnight Sun**.
 
• Consequently, among the given options, the latitude at **66½degree N** experiences the maximum possible daylight duration (24 hours), making it the longest compared to lower northern latitudes or any southern latitudes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equator (0 degree):**

 
 
• Experiences nearly **equal day and night** (approximately 12 hours each) throughout the year regardless of the solstice.
 
 
 
• **Tropic of Cancer (23½degree N):**
 
 
• Receives **overhead sunlight** at noon during the June solstice.
 
• Daylight lasts approximately **13.5 hours**, which is long but significantly less than the 24 hours at the Arctic Circle.
 
 
 
• **Tropic of Capricorn (23½degree S):**
 
 
• Experiences the **Winter Solstice** during June.
 
• It has the **shortest day** of the year in the Southern Hemisphere, with daylight lasting roughly 10.5 hours.

• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** was enacted by the **Indian Parliament** to provide for the acquisition and determination of Indian citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.
 
• While **Articles 5 to 10** of the **Constitution of India** dealt with citizenship at the time of its commencement, **Article 11** specifically empowered the Parliament to regulate the right of citizenship by law.
 
• The Act outlines five distinct methods to acquire Indian citizenship: **By Birth**, **By Descent**, **By Registration**, **By Naturalization**, and **By Incorporation of Territory** (e.g., when **Pondicherry** became part of India).
 
• It also defines three specific ways through which citizenship can be lost: **Renunciation** (voluntary giving up), **Termination** (automatic loss upon acquiring another country's citizenship), and **Deprivation** (compulsory termination by the government for fraud or disloyalty).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Constitution of India** does not provide for **Dual Citizenship**; it only recognizes **Single Citizenship** for the entire country to promote national integration.
 
• The **Citizenship Act, 1955** has undergone several significant amendments to adapt to evolving socio-political requirements:
 
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1986**: Implemented stricter criteria for citizenship by birth to curb illegal immigration, particularly in **Assam**.
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2003**: Introduced the concept of **Overseas Citizenship of India (OCI)** for Persons of Indian Origin (PIOs) in certain countries and defined 'illegal migrants'.
 
• **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019**: Provided a pathway to Indian citizenship for persecuted religious minorities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians) from **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, and **Pakistan** who entered India on or before **December 31, 2014**.
 
 
 
• Citizenship falls under the **Union List** in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution, meaning only the **Central Government** (Ministry of Home Affairs) has the jurisdiction to legislate on it.

questions.question: Which memory is fastest and located inside the CPU?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Registers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Registers** are the smallest and fastest storage units in a computer system, directly integrated into the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**.
 
• They operate at the same speed as the **processor clock**, providing near-instantaneous access to data for **arithmetic**, **logical**, and **control** operations.
 
• Located inside the **CPU core**, they hold specific items like the **Program Counter (PC)**, **Instruction Register (IR)**, and **Accumulator**, facilitating the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
 
• Because they are part of the internal **ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit)** and **Control Unit** circuitry, they have the lowest latency of any memory type in the **memory hierarchy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hard Disk:**

 
 
• It is a **secondary storage** device used for high-capacity, non-volatile data storage.
 
• It is significantly slower than internal CPU memory because it connects via external interfaces like **SATA** and may involve mechanical movement.
 
 
 
• **Cache L3:**
 
 
• **Level 3 (L3) Cache** is a specialized high-speed memory that acts as a buffer between **RAM** and **L1/L2 caches**.
 
• While it is typically located on the **CPU die**, it is shared across multiple cores and is slower than the dedicated **Registers** and **L1 Cache**.
 
 
 
• **RAM (Random Access Memory):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **main memory**, it is a volatile storage area that holds the OS and active applications.
 
• It is located on the **motherboard** and communicates with the CPU via the **Memory Controller** and **System Bus**, resulting in higher latency than on-chip caches or registers.

questions.question: *Chhau, a celebrated dance tradition from Eastern India, has been acknowledged by UNESCO under which cultural recognition category?*

__
 
• **Chhau dance** is a vibrant tradition from **Eastern India** that was officially inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity** in **2010**.
 
• It is predominantly practiced in three distinct sub-styles named after their geographic origins: **Seraikella Chhau** in Jharkhand, **Purulia Chhau** in West Bengal, and **Mayurbhanj Chhau** in Odisha.
 
• The dance is a unique blend of **martial arts**, acrobatics, and storytelling, often depicting episodes from great Indian epics such as the **Ramayana** and the **Mahabharata**, as well as abstract themes like the cycle of seasons.
 
• While the **Seraikella** and **Purulia** styles are known for the use of elaborate **masks** that represent the characters, the **Mayurbhanj** style is performed without masks, relying instead on facial expressions and body movements.
 
• The performance is traditionally accompanied by rhythmic music played on folk instruments such as the **Mohuri** (reed instrument) and various drums like the **Dhol**, **Dhumsa**, and **Nagada**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Understanding Cultural Recognitions**

 
 
• **Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH)**:

 
 
• This category refers to the **practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, and skills** that communities recognize as part of their cultural heritage.
 
• It was established by the **UNESCO 2003 Convention** to safeguard living heritage such as **Vedic Chanting**, **Kumbh Mela**, and **Yoga**.
 
 
 
• **World Heritage Sites**:
 
 
• Governed by the **1972 Convention**, this category recognizes tangible locations like **monuments**, **buildings**, or **natural sites** of outstanding universal value.
 
• Examples include the **Ajanta Caves**, **Sun Temple Konark**, and **Western Ghats**.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Landscape Heritage**:
 
 
• A sub-classification under World Heritage Sites that focuses on the **human-nature interaction** and the evolution of human society under the influence of physical constraints or opportunities of their **natural environment**.

questions.question: Which river system supports Bangladesh’s extreme population density?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta**, also known as the **Ganges Delta** or the **Bengal Delta**, is the largest river delta in the world, spanning approximately **105,000 square kilometers**.
 
• It is formed by the confluence of three major rivers: the **Ganges** (known as the **Padma** in Bangladesh), the **Brahmaputra** (known as the **Jamuna**), and the **Meghna**, which empty into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The delta is composed of highly fertile **alluvial soil**. Annual monsoon flooding deposits nutrient-rich **silt** across the plains, creating some of the most productive agricultural land on Earth.
 
• This immense agricultural productivity, particularly for **rice** and **jute**, provides the food security necessary to support **Bangladesh’s** extreme population density, which exceeds **1,200 persons per square kilometer**.
 
• Approximately **two-thirds** of the delta lies within **Bangladesh**, making the country almost entirely dependent on this river system for its economy, transport, and water supply.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

• Located in **Northeast Africa**, it supports the majority of **Egypt’s** population.
 
• While it historically facilitated high population concentrations, it is geologically distinct and unrelated to the geography of **South Asia**.
 
 
 
• **Amazon River Basin**:
 
 
• Located in **South America**, it is the largest drainage basin in the world by discharge volume.
 
• Despite its size, it remains one of the most sparsely populated regions due to the dense **Amazon Rainforest** and leached, acidic soils.
 
 
 
• **Mississippi River Plain**:
 
 
• Located in the **United States**, it serves as a critical agricultural hub for **North America**.
 
• It utilizes high-tech industrial farming rather than the high-density subsistence and intensive labor farming seen in the **Ganges Delta**.

questions.question: In Arthashastra, which two types of courts dealt with disputes among citizens and between the state and citizens?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dharmasthiya and Kantakashodhana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arthashastra**, written by **Kautilya** (Chanakya), provides a detailed blueprint of the **Mauryan administration**, including a specialized two-tier judicial system.
 
• **Dharmasthiya** courts were essentially **civil courts** that adjudicated disputes related to **Vyavahara** (legal procedures), covering matters like marriage, inheritance, **debt**, deposits, and labor disputes among citizens.
 
• The **Kantakashodhana** courts, meaning **removal of thorns**, functioned as **criminal and administrative courts** to protect the state and society from anti-social elements and bureaucratic corruption.
 
• The **Dharmasthiya** courts were presided over by three **Dharmasthas** (experts in sacred law), while **Kantakashodhana** courts were managed by three **Pradeshtris** (commissioners) who dealt with crimes such as theft, murder, and treason.
 
• These courts were established at various administrative levels, including the **Sangrahana**, **Dronamukha**, **Sthaniya**, and **Janapada Sandhi**, ensuring justice was accessible throughout the **Mauryan Empire**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sabha and Samiti**:

 
 
• These were representative assemblies of the **Vedic Period**. The **Sabha** was an elite council of elders, while the **Samiti** was a broader assembly of the common people (**Vis**).
 
 
 
• **Sangha and Gana**:
 
 
• These terms refer to **republican or oligarchic polities** (**Gana-Sanghas**) that existed in ancient India, such as the **Vrijji** or **Shakyas**, where governance was shared among multiple chiefs.
 
 
 
• **Mantriparishad**:
 
 
• This was the **Council of Ministers** in the Mauryan state, which assisted the **King** in executive duties and policy implementation, as specified in **Kautilya's** administrative structure.

questions.question: Which inscription expresses Ashoka’s remorse after the Kalinga war?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rock Edict XIII**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rock Edict XIII** is considered the most significant and the longest of the **fourteen Major Rock Edicts** issued by **Emperor Ashoka** of the **Maurya Dynasty**.
 
• This edict provides a detailed account of the **Kalinga War**, which occurred in the **8th year** of Ashoka's coronation, approximately in **261 BCE**.
 
• It records the profound **remorse** (anutapa) and **repentance** felt by the Emperor after witnessing the massive scale of destruction, where **100,000** people were killed and **150,000** were deported.
 
• The inscription describes how the suffering of **Brahmins**, **Shramanas**, and householders moved Ashoka to abandon **Sastra-vijaya** (conquest by force) in favor of **Dhamma-vijaya** (conquest by righteousness).
 
• It is historically vital as it mentions five **Greek (Yona) kings**: **Antiochus II** of Syria, **Ptolemy II** of Egypt, **Antigonus Gonatas** of Macedonia, **Magas** of Cyrene, and **Alexander** of Epirus, confirming the international reach of Ashoka's **Dhamma**.
 
• The edict concludes with an appeal to his successors to forgo further military conquests and instead focus on the spread of moral conduct and piety.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other Major Edicts:**

 
 
• **Rock Edict I**: Primarily focuses on the prohibition of **animal sacrifices** and festive gatherings; it mentions that the slaughter of animals in the royal kitchen was significantly reduced.
 
• **Rock Edict VII**: Emphasizes **religious tolerance** and harmony among all sects, stating that all religions desire self-control and purity of mind.
 
• **Pillar Edict V**: Also known as the **Delhi-Topra Pillar Edict**, it provides a comprehensive list of animals, birds, and fish that were granted protection from killing on specific days.

__
 
• **Rani Lakshmi Bai**, originally named **Manikarnika Tambe**, was the queen of the Maratha-ruled princely state of **Jhansi**.
 
• She became a legendary figure in Indian history for her pivotal role in the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, resisting British colonial rule.
 
• The conflict between the Rani and the British intensified after the death of her husband, **Maharaja Gangadhar Rao**, when the British refused to recognize her adopted son, **Damodar Rao**, as the legitimate heir.
 
• Following the siege of **Jhansi Fort** by British forces in early **1858**, she made a daring escape and joined forces with other rebel leaders, including **Tatya Tope**.
 
• The Rani and her troops successfully captured the **Gwalior Fort** from the Scindias, who were British allies, making it a major stronghold for the rebels.
 
• She was killed in battle on **June 18, 1858**, while fighting the British **8th Hussars** at **Kotah-ki-Serai** near Gwalior.
 
• The British commander, **Sir Hugh Rose**, who led the campaign against her, remarkably praised her as the **'bravest and best military leader'** of the rebellion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Doctrine of Lapse**:

 
 
• An annexation policy devised by **Lord Dalhousie**, the **Governor-General of India** between **1848** and **1856**.
 
• Under this policy, any princely state under the direct or indirect (paramount) control of the **British East India Company** where the ruler did not have a legal male heir would be annexed by the company.
 
 
 
• **Sir Hugh Rose**:
 
 
• The senior British Army officer who commanded the **Central India Field Force**.
 
• He was responsible for the suppression of the revolt in central India, including the capture of **Jhansi** and **Gwalior**.
 
 
 
• **Gwalior Campaign**:
 
 
• The final major phase of the **1857 Revolt** in Central India where the Rani died, leading to the eventual restoration of British control over the region.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Parliamentary Committee in India?

options.text: To examine bills and policies in detail
To supervise elections across the country
To appoint ministers to executive offices
To amend provisions of the Constitution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To examine bills and policies in detail**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parliamentary Committees** are established because the **Indian Parliament** is a large body with a vast workload and limited time, making it impossible to discuss every **Bill** or **Policy** in exhaustive detail on the floor of the House.
 
• These committees function as 'mini-parliaments' where members from different political parties deliberate in a non-partisan environment to provide **Legislative Oversight** over the **Executive**.
 
• The primary purpose is to undertake a **technical and detailed scrutiny** of legislative proposals, **budgetary allocations**, and departmental expenditures to ensure efficiency and accountability.
 
• They derive their authority from **Article 105** (privileges of members) and **Article 118** (power of each House to make rules for regulating its procedure) of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• Committees have the power to summon **Government Officials**, experts, and stakeholders to gather evidence, which helps in refining **Public Policy** before it is finalized.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Committees**:

 
 
• **Standing Committees**: These are permanent committees constituted annually. Examples include **Financial Committees** like the **Public Accounts Committee**, **Estimates Committee**, and **Committee on Public Undertakings**.
 
• **Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs)**: There are **24** such committees (16 for **Lok Sabha** and 8 for **Rajya Sabha**) that examine the **Demands for Grants** of various ministries.
 
• **Ad-hoc Committees**: Temporary committees created for a specific task, such as a **Select Committee** or a **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC)**, which dissolve after submitting their report.
 
 
 
• **Election Supervision**: This is the mandate of the **Election Commission of India**, an independent constitutional body established under **Article 324**, not a parliamentary committee.
 
• **Ministerial Appointments**: **Ministers** are appointed by the **President of India** on the advice of the **Prime Minister** under **Article 75**; committees play no role in executive appointments.
 
• **Constitutional Amendments**: The power to amend the **Constitution** lies with the **Parliament** (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) through the process defined in **Article 368**, requiring specific majorities.
